---
title: "Released data behind the evidence pages"
subtitle: "Catalog A-13 · data lineage and licence"
description: "Every summary table the site reads, with its source in the replication package, its level, its size and its fixed caption."
toc: false
---

The evidence pages read summary tables that the replication package
([joonho112/DPprior-paper-replication](https://github.com/joonho112/DPprior-paper-replication))
releases. They are copied, not recomputed: no MCMC runs in the browser, and no pupil-level,
response-level or individual posterior-draw data are included. A contract file records each
table's source, level, rows, columns, sha256 and licence scope, and the site's verification
gate (`verification/check_data_contract.mjs`) fails if a table changes, loses or gains a
column, contains an individual-level field, or lacks its rights statement.

**What CC BY 4.0 covers.** The grant covers the author's contribution and nothing more. The simulation and calibration tables are the author's own output and are
covered whole. The application tables hold the author's posterior summaries of data that
belong to others, and the per-unit inputs in `star_units.json` and `bd_units.json` (the
estimate `tau_hat`, its standard error `se` and the size `n_j`) come straight from those data:
Project STAR through the R package mlmRev, and Bangert-Drowns, Hurley and Wilkinson (2004)
through the R package metadat. Both packages are distributed under GPL (>= 2), a package
licence rather than a separate grant for the original study data, so these inputs keep their
upstream terms and are not relicensed here. The vocabulary tables derive from an Item Response
Warehouse table whose derived licence is CC BY 4.0, subject to upstream rights (collected by
the Open-Source Psychometrics Project; scale by Brotherton, French and Pickering, 2013). Each card
below states its table's scope, upstream source and terms, following the replication
package's `LICENSE-SCOPE.md` and `provenance/data-rights.csv`.

One table is the declared exception: `rasch_respondents.json` holds anonymous derived values
for the 500 respondents of the vocabulary application (row number, raw score, WLE, its SE
and a perfect-score flag), re-derived from the public Item Response Warehouse table with the
replication package's sampling rule and scoring code. It has no responses and no source IDs,
it is the only file on the respondent-level allowlist, and the gate checks that it agrees
with the score-group table (the same count, WLE and SE at every raw score).

```{=html}
<div id="w-lineage" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/data-lineage-card.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = { dataBase: "../../data/released/" };
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    window.__dpxLineage = DPX["data-lineage-card"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-lineage"), spec);
  })();
</script>
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Simulation summaries keep the paper's retained-fit denominators: 8,607 of 9,000 planned fits
in the 45 main cells (57,151 of 64,400 across all suites). The replication package's OCRS
application (descriptive school-level contrasts, not the original blocked intent-to-treat
analysis) is not used on this site.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/data-lineage-card.html](../../embed/data-lineage-card.html) (for example `?preset=rasch`).
